items.item_text: Bachelor of Science degree life/biomedical science discipline, or equivalent experience
Working knowledge and experience in general immunology, cell biology and molecular and biology techniques.
Prior experience in oncology biomedical research.
The candidate will work as a full-time Staff Research Associate II (SRA II) in a cutting-edge regenerative medicine research laboratory under the mentorship of Dr. Gerald Lipshutz.

More specifically, the SRA II will primarily work on a mouse model of metabolic disease, using a gene therapy treatment to correct the abnormality and analysis of organs, blood and tissues for expression levels. The candidate will perform a variety of routine experimental protocols and procedures at a fully operational level, including but not limited to, animal experiments, use of human specimens, cell and tissue culture, DNA/RNA/genomic DNA extraction, ELISA and western blots. The SRA II will also take on a significant portion of the lab management duties, including supply management, ordering, and equipment maintenance and calibration. The candidate will also coordinate and assist with general lab support activities (e.g. making common lab reagents). The SRA II candidate will have some supervisory responsibilities as the day-to-day manager of the undergraduate students and other part-time members of the Lipshutz Lab.
Ability to use computer software for word processing, data tabulation and graphing.
Ability and knowledge to operate basic laboratory equipment, i.e. centrifuge, tissue culture hood and related equipment, autoclaving, weighing, pipetting microliter volumes, etc.
Knowledge of cell culture and sterile techniques.
Ability and working knowledge of DNA, RNA, protein purification and quantification; PCR, qPCR, Western Blot.
Excellent communication skills to interact with other researchers, vendors, suppliers, and maintenance engineers.
Ability to perform tasks accurately and in a timely manner working independently under the program guidelines and under frequent changes in priorities and deadlines
Knowledge and ability to order supplies and maintain laboratory equipment.
Ability to generate hypotheses, suggest experimental designs, interpret data and recognize aberrant results.
